description: A group of friends who are passionate about computer science and software
summary:
TerraRotation is an agricultural decision-support platform created by RO Team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The challenge it addresses is called "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data."

Our solution takes NASA climate data and global soil information. Turns it into useful location-specific crop rotation plans.

By using NASA POWER and ISRIC SoilGrids TerraRotation lets farmers choose fields look at environmental conditions create crop rotation plans for many years and see how those plans might work under different climate situations.

TerraRotation is different from tools that suggest crops. It focuses on long-term farming planning. Its decision-support engine looks at rotation options takes into account the rules of farming explains the choices it makes and helps with planning when conditions change.
Features like Climate Stress Lab, Rotation DNA and Confidence Engine help users see not which rotation plans might work but also the risks to the environment the trade-offs involved and how sure we can be, about the data.
TerraRotation wants to connect Earth data with daily farming choices. It helps farmers create resilient and sustainable ways to grow crops.
details:
TerraRotation. Smarter Crop Rotation with NASA Data

The Problem

Farming is becoming more unpredictable. Weather changes, hot days and soil problems make it harder to plan crops well.

Farmers must think beyond the harvest. What they plant today changes soil health, future yields and the choices that will be available later.

Crop rotation can solve these problems. Making a good plan needs climate, soil, crop fit and long‑term risks. The data is there but turning it into useful decisions is not always easy.

Our Solution

We built TerraRotation to make long‑term crop planning simpler and more accessible.

By combining climate data from NASA POWER with soil information from ISRIC SoilGrids TerraRotation helps users create, compare and adjust crop rotation plans.

Of only suggesting what to grow next TerraRotation looks at how different crops work together over time and how changing environmental conditions might affect those plans.

How It Works

1. Select a Field

Users can choose a location on a map, type coordinates or draw field boundaries.

2. Analyze the Environment

TerraRotation pulls climate data from NASA POWER and soil data from ISRIC SoilGrids to check conditions at the chosen location.

3. Generate Crop Rotations

Our Rotation Engine builds multi‑year crop sequences taking into account climate suitability and crop relationships. It compares options to show strengths and trade‑offs.

4. Test Climate Scenarios

Climate Stress Lab tests rotation plans against four climate scenarios helping users see how their choices might perform as conditions change.

5.. Understand Results

Rotation DNA gives a five‑dimensional profile of each plan while Confidence Engine points out missing or incomplete data. Users can see why a rotation was recommended and where uncertainty remains.

6. Adapt the Plan

With Adaptive Rotation users can update their plans after a growing season without starting the process again.

Technology

We developed TerraRotation using:

  • Python for main analysing algorithm, data processing and rotation analysis.
    FastAPI for the backend
  • React for the interface and field selection.
  • Electron for desktop integration.
  • NASA POWER for climate and meteorological data.
  • ISRIC SoilGrids for soil information.

The application brings these parts together in one workflow from field selection to exploring crop rotation recommendations.

What Makes TerraRotation Different?

TerraRotation is not another crop recommendation tool.

It combines long‑term planning, climate scenario testing, multi‑criteria evaluation and explainable results in one application.

Users can compare strategies understand why recommendations are made and see how reliable the data is.

Our goal was not to create another scientific dashboard. We wanted to make environmental data truly useful, for decisions.

Impact and Future Plans

TerraRotation aims to help farmers and agricultural advisers make better‑informed decisions understand climate risks and plan sustainable crop rotations.

It is still a prototype and its recommendations are meant to support expertise rather than replace it.

In the future we want to add environmental datasets, economic analysis and validation using real‑world farming results.

TerraRotation turns Earth data into farming decisions.
